Subject: Sandbox prolongation & credit request — SDK instrumentation rewrite

Hi Ava,

Quick note following our demo last week — Streamline’s engineers uncovered an unexpected dependency on our telemetry v2 headers when exercising the SDK in your staging environment. Dylan’s team dug in and concluded the current SDK instrumentation needs a small rewrite (affects initialization and retry paths) before the connector can run reliably at scale.

Impact: engineering estimates ~5 business days for a targeted hotfix + one canary iteration. Procurement timeline you mentioned depends on us keeping the sandbox active during that work.

Suggested remedy from our side:
- 14-day extension of your sandbox access after today
- 40k token goodwill credit applied to the pilot account (can use for demo load and one full canary)
- We’ll provide a short MOU addendum for signatures to document the extension and credit.

I attached an integration_preview.log that Dylan pulled from your staging run. Can you confirm this timeline works and whether procurement needs a formal SOW tweak? If helpful I can loop in Marissa for commercial wording.

Thanks — want to keep momentum here.

—Markus

2) a small token credit so our QA can finish one full canary without throttling.

If you can get the 14-day extension and 30–40k token credit documented, procurement will greenlight quickly. I attached the error_stack.txt we captured.

Subject: RE: Sandbox prolongation & credit request — SDK instrumentation rewrite

Looping in technical details so commercial can decide:

Root cause summary: the SDK’s startup path was assuming legacy telemetry headers; when Streamline’s infra injects a proxy with rewrite rules the retry timer doesn’t initialize and we get a null reference on the first RPC. Fix is straightforward but touches init and the backoff util.

Workplan:
- Day 0–1: repro + unit tests
- Day 2–3: patch + integration tests in our staging harness
- Day 4: deploy hotfix to canary and validate with Streamline test vectors
- Day 5: release candidate and handoff notes

ETA: 5 business days from kick-off. Risk: minimal, but we need Streamline to run a short canary (~1 hour) to validate.

Recommendation for commercial: offer 14-day sandbox prolongation and 40k token credit (we want the canary to succeed — 30k risks another partial run). I’ll prioritize the patch if you approve.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
